assignedReviews.card_evidence: the first microsatellite built by Filipinos to take pictures of our country from space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a Filipino-built invention (Diwata-1) but does not identify a specific scientist, which is the core action of the competency. It only mentions that Filipinos built it, not a named scientist and their invention.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the first microsatellite built by Filipinos to take pictures of our country from space
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from the home or the local community to identify a science invention and explain its impact on their everyday life
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a science invention but does not explain its impact on everyday life, and the source is not from home or the local community. The stated purpose (taking pictures) is not an impact on daily life.

copy.en: Launched in 2016, Diwata-1 was the first microsatellite built by Filipinos to take pictures of our country from space!
copy.tl: Inilunsad noong 2016, ang Diwata-1 ang unang microsatellite na ginawa ng mga Pilipino para kumuha ng larawan ng bansa mula sa space!
copy.bis: Gilusad niadtong 2016, ang Diwata-1 mao ang unang microsatellite nga gibuhat sa mga Pilipino aron magkuha og hulagway sa nasod gikan sa space!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thick rock and soil sit between us and the hot part below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to name and describe the upper crustal layers of the solid earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rock and soil but does not name or describe upper crustal layers, nor does it involve gathering information from secondary sources. It only touches on the general idea of Earth's interior.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Thick rock and soil sit between us and the hot part below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: create a scale drawing to represent relative thicknesses of the layers of Earth's interior, including the crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, and inner core
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to the hot part below and intervening rock/soil, but it does not create a scale drawing or represent relative thicknesses of Earth's interior layers. It does not name any of the required layers (crust, lithosphere, asthenosphere, mantle, outer core, inner core).

copy.en: Why don't we feel the heat under our feet? Thick rock and soil sit between us and the hot part below, so the heat never reaches the surface!
copy.tl: Bakit hindi natin nararamdaman ang init sa paa? Makapal na bato at lupa ang nasa pagitan natin at ng mainit na bahagi, kaya hindi umaabot ang init sa ibabaw!
copy.bis: Ngano dili nato mabati ang init sa tiil? Bagang bato ug yuta ang naa sa tunga nato ug sa init nga bahin, mao nga dili moabot ang init sa ibabaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Is it safe to build a power plant near a volcano?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use local information or other reliable sources to identify where the nearest active and inactive volcanoes are located and assess the risk of impacts from eruptions to their local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses safety of building a power plant near a volcano, but does not identify locations of active/inactive volcanoes or assess eruption risks to the local community as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Is it safe to build a power plant near a volcano?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe volcano types by activity, eruption type, or location in the crust; it only addresses general safety of geothermal plants near volcanoes.

copy.en:
Is it safe to build a power plant near a volcano?

Yes! Engineers study the volcano carefully, pick the safest spots, and always monitor it — so the plant can operate safely without any danger.
copy.tl:
Ligtas ba ang magtayo ng power plant malapit sa bulkan?

Oo! Pinag-aaralan ng mga inhinyero ang bulkan nang maigi, pinipili ang pinakaligtas na lugar, at lagi itong binabantayan — kaya ligtas itong gumana.
copy.bis:
Luwas ba ang magtukod og power plant duol sa bulkan?

Oo! Gitun-an sa mga inhenyero ang bulkan pag-ayo, mopili sila sa pinakaluwas nga lugar, ug kanunay kini gibantayan — mao nga luwas kining modagan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our thousands of islands include little sandbars and rocks poking out of the sea.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions islands and rocks as landforms, but does not describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment, which is the core of G5-E-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Our thousands of islands include little sandbars and rocks poking out of the sea.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions rocks but does not involve observing or collecting different types of rocks or describing their features (texture, color, grain crystal size). It only notes that some islands are tiny rocks, which is not direct support for G5-E-2.

copy.en:
Are all Philippine islands huge?

Nope! While Luzon is huge, many islands are as tiny as a small field! Our thousands of islands include little sandbars and rocks poking out of the sea.
copy.tl:
Laki ba lahat ng isla sa Pilipinas?

Hindi! Kahit malaki ang Luzon, maraming isla na kasingliit lang ng maliit na bukid! Kasama sa libu-libong isla natin ang mga munting sandbar at bato.
copy.bis:
Dagko ba tanang isla sa Pilipinas?

Dili! Bisan dagko ang Luzon, daghan ang isla nga kagamay ra sa usa ka gamayng uma! Apil sa libo-libong isla ang gagmayng balas ug bato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines is an archipelago, meaning it is made up of thousands of islands surrounded by water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that the Philippines is an archipelago of thousands of islands surrounded by water. It does not identify specific local landforms or bodies of water (mountains, valleys, rivers, coastlines) nor describe how they influence living and non-living components, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: The Philippines is an archipelago, meaning it is made up of thousands of islands surrounded by water!
copy.tl: Ang Pilipinas ay isang arkipelago, ibig sabihin ito ay binubuo ng libu-libong isla na napapaligiran ng tubig!
copy.bis: Ang Pilipinas usa ka arkipelago, nagpasabot nga kini gilangkoban sa liboan ka isla nga gipalibutan sa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it's still around 20 degrees!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and appropriately use units in simple science activities, such as milligrams (mg), grams (g), kilograms (kg), and degrees centigrade (C)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions degrees as a temperature measure but does not teach identifying or appropriately using units in a science activity. It does not name the unit (degrees centigrade) or demonstrate its use in measurement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 0 degrees needed to make ice or snow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card references freezing (ice/snow) but does not describe changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) using diagrams or flowcharts. It only mentions a temperature threshold, not the process or required representation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: 0 degrees needed to make ice or snow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that 0 degrees is needed for ice or snow, touching on temperature causing a state change, but it does not describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It lacks explanation of the process.

copy.en: Even when the amihan season feels chilly, it's still around 20 degrees! That's far from the 0 degrees needed to make ice or snow.
copy.tl: Kahit malamig tuwing amihan, nasa 20 degrees pa rin! Malayo pa iyon sa 0 degrees na kailangan para magkaroon ng yelo o niyebe.
copy.bis: Bisan tugnawon panahon sa amihan, mga 20 degrees gihapon! Layo pa na sa 0 degrees nga gikinahanglan aron mo-yelo o mo-niyebe.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The Philippines has no winter because it lies in the tropics!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different seasons in the Philippines and suggest activities that are appropriate for each season
assignedReviews.reason: The card only explains why the Philippines has no winter due to its tropical location near the equator. It does not describe the different seasons in the Philippines or suggest activities appropriate for each season, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It is near the equator, so it stays warm all year.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Philippines being near the equator and staying warm, which touches on sunlight intensity, but it does not demonstrate how Earth's tilt relative to its orbit affects sunlight intensity over a year, nor does it use a physical model or drawings. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Why doesn't the Philippines have a winter season?

The Philippines has no winter because it lies in the tropics! It is near the equator, so it stays warm all year.
copy.tl:
Bakit walang taglamig ang Pilipinas?

Walang taglamig sa Pilipinas dahil nasa tropiko tayo! Malapit tayo sa ekwador, kaya mainit buong taon.
copy.bis:
Nganong walay tingtugnaw ang Pilipinas?

Walay tingtugnaw sa Pilipinas kay naa man mi sa tropiko! Duol mi sa ekwador, maong init tibuok tuig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the strong amihan and habagat monsoon winds can be a source of wind energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw on information from secondary sources to identify situations where tidal difference could be exploited to generate renewable energy
assignedReviews.reason: The competency specifically targets tidal difference as a renewable energy source. The card discusses wind energy from monsoons, not tidal energy, so it does not directly support the stated skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the strong amihan and habagat monsoon winds can be a source of wind energy
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to evaluate how renewable and non-renewable generation of electricity in the Philippines impacts human activities and the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires evaluating how renewable and non-renewable electricity generation impacts human activities and the environment. The card only states that monsoon winds can be a source of wind energy; it does not evaluate impacts on human activities or the environment.

copy.en:
Can our local winds make energy?

In the Philippines, the strong amihan and habagat monsoon winds can be a source of wind energy!
copy.tl:
Pwede bang gumawa ng enerhiya ang hangin natin?

Sa Pilipinas, ang malalakas na hanging amihan at habagat ay puwedeng pagkunan ng enerhiya ng hangin!
copy.bis:
Mahimong makahimo og enerhiya ang atong hangin?

Sa Pilipinas, ang kusog nga amihan ug habagat nga hangin mahimong tinubdan sa enerhiya sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: PHIVOLCS is the Philippine agency that carefully monitors volcanoes and earthquakes to issue important safety warnings!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: Interpret PHIVOLCS Volcano Monitoring (Alert Levels) to demonstrate what to do before, during, and after a volcanic eruption
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that PHIVOLCS monitors volcanoes and earthquakes to issue warnings. It does not mention alert levels, interpretation, or actions before/during/after an eruption, so it does not directly support the competency.

copy.en: PHIVOLCS is the Philippine agency that carefully monitors volcanoes and earthquakes to issue important safety warnings!
copy.tl: Ang PHIVOLCS ang ahensya ng Pilipinas na nagmamatyag sa mga bulkan at lindol para magbigay ng babala!
copy.bis: Ang PHIVOLCS mao ang ahensya sa Pilipinas nga nagbantay sa mga bulkan ug linog aron maghatag og pasidaan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Some plants sense day length to know when to flower
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a specific advanced example of a plant response (photoperiodism) and flowering, but it does not teach the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) at the Grade 3 level. It is a specialized topic that goes beyond the scope of the competency, which expects students to describe these characteristics in simple terms. The card shares vocabulary (respond, reproduce) but does not directly support the competency's instructional goal.

copy.en: Some plants sense day length to know when to flower—short-day plants like rice bloom only when nights are long, while others bloom when nights are short.
copy.tl: May kakayahan ang mga halaman na maramdaman ang haba ng araw at gabi para malaman kung kailan mamumukadkad—ang short-day plants tulad ng palay ay namumukadkad lang kapag mahaba ang gabi, habang ang iba ay namumukadkad kapag maikli ang gabi.
copy.bis: Adunay katakos ang mga tanom nga maramdaman ang haba sa adlaw ug gabii aron mahibaloan kung kanus-a mamukadkad—ang short-day plants sama sa palay mamukadkad lamang kung dugay ang gabii, samtang ang uban mamukadkad kung mubo ang gabii.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because photosynthesis needs light! It runs faster in bright light, but slows down in shade or darkness since there's less light to use.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that light affects the rate of photosynthesis. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials or products, so it does not directly support G8-L-9.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because photosynthesis needs light!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions light as a need for plants, but G3-L-6 focuses on basic needs such as air, food, water, and shelter. Light is not among the listed needs, and the card does not address the general basic needs of all living things.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do plants grow slower in shade?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about light affecting photosynthesis rate, not about the root and shoot system of plants or their importance. It does not support G4-L-2.

copy.en:
Why do plants grow slower in shade?

Because photosynthesis needs light! It runs faster in bright light, but slows down in shade or darkness since there's less light to use.
copy.tl:
Bakit mabagal lumaki ang halaman sa lilim?

Dahil kailangan ng photosynthesis ang liwanag! Mas mabilis ito kapag maliwanag, pero bumabagal sa lilim o dilim dahil kulang ang liwanag.
copy.bis:
Ngano hinay motubo ang tanom sa landong?

Kay ang photosynthesis nagkinahanglan og kahayag! Mas paspas kini kung hayag, apan mohinay sa landong o kangitngit kay kulang ang kahayag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they make their own food using sunlight, a process called photosynthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that plants make food using sunlight and names the process photosynthesis. It does not describe the process, identify raw materials (water, carbon dioxide) or products (glucose, oxygen), nor mention respiration. This is basic background knowledge, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en:
How do plants make food?

Plants don't eat like we do — they make their own food using sunlight, a process called photosynthesis.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagawa ng pagkain ang halaman?

Hindi kumakain ang halaman tulad natin — gumagawa sila ng sariling pagkain gamit ang liwanag ng araw, na tinatawag na photosynthesis.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paghimo sa tanom sa iyang pagkaon?

Ang tanom dili mokaon sama nato — naghimo sila og kaugalingong pagkaon gamit ang kahayag sa adlaw, nga gitawag og photosynthesis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most phytoplankton are so tiny that you can't see them at all without a microscope.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a characteristic of phytoplankton (microscopic size) but does not use a table or classify living things into the named groups required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most phytoplankton are so tiny that you can't see them at all without a microscope.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the parts and functions, and demonstrate proper handling and storing of a compound microscope
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes that a microscope is needed to see phytoplankton; it does not identify parts and functions of a compound microscope or demonstrate handling and storing.

copy.en: Most phytoplankton are so tiny that you can't see them at all without a microscope.
copy.tl: Napakaliit ng karamihan sa phytoplankton kaya hindi mo sila makikita nang walang mikroskopyo.
copy.bis: Gagmay kaayo ang kadaghanan sa phytoplankton mao nga dili nimo makita kon wala ka mikroskopyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother pig stays pregnant for about 114 days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives the gestation duration for a pig but does not identify that pigs are mammals that give birth to live young, nor does it contrast live birth with egg-laying. It only touches on reproduction indirectly.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A mother pig stays pregnant for about 114 days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions pregnancy, which is part of reproduction, but it does not describe the characteristic of reproduction (or growth/response) in living things. It provides a specific fact about gestation length rather than teaching the general characteristic.

copy.en: A mother pig stays pregnant for about 114 days — easy to remember as three months, three weeks, and three days.
copy.tl: Nagbubuntis ang inahing baboy nang halos 114 araw — madaling tandaan bilang tatlong buwan, tatlong linggo, at tatlong araw.
copy.bis: Ang inahang baboy mabdos og mga 114 ka adlaw — sayon hinumdoman nga tulo ka bulan, tulo ka semana, ug tulo ka adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A pig is pregnant for about 114 days
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific gestation length for a pig but does not identify pigs as mammals that give birth to live young, nor contrast them with egg-laying groups. It does not directly support the competency's classification skill.

copy.en: A pig is pregnant for about 114 days — around 3 months and 3 weeks.
copy.tl: Nagbubuntis ang baboy nang mga 114 araw — mga 3 buwan at 3 linggo.
copy.bis: Ang baboy magmabdos sulod sa mga 114 ka adlaw — mga 3 ka bulan ug 3 ka semana.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: unlike true deer, the pilandok has no antlers
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: unlike true deer, the pilandok has no antlers. Instead, males have small tusks poking out from the mouth
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: Antlers versus tusks is not the difference between animals with a backbone and animals without backbones.

copy.en:
Does the pilandok have antlers like a deer?

No — unlike true deer, the pilandok has no antlers. Instead, males have small tusks poking out from the mouth.
copy.tl:
May sungay ba ang pilandok tulad ng usa?

Wala — hindi tulad ng ibang usa, walang sungay ang pilandok. Sa halip, may maliliit na pangil ang lalaki na lumalabas sa nguso.
copy.bis:
Naa bay sungay ang pilandok sama sa usa?

Wala — dili sama sa tinuod nga usa, ang pilandok walay sungay. Hinuon, ang lalaki adunay gagmayng pangil nga mosungaw sa baba.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It erupted powerfully in Zambales and temporarily cooled the whole planet's temperature!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single volcanic eruption (Pinatubo 1991) and its global cooling effect. It does not describe different types of volcanoes according to activity, eruption type, or location in the crust, nor does it classify Pinatubo within those categories. The mention of 'erupted powerfully' is too vague to support the competency's classification of eruption types.

copy.en:
What happened when Mount Pinatubo erupted in 1991?

It erupted powerfully in Zambales and temporarily cooled the whole planet's temperature!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyari nang sumabog ang Bulkang Pinatubo noong 1991?

Sumabog ito nang malakas sa Zambales at nagpalamig pansamantala sa temperatura ng buong mundo!
copy.bis:
Unsay nahitabo nang mibuto ang Bulkang Pinatubo niadtong 1991?

Kusog kini nga mibuto sa Zambales ug temporaryong nakapabugnaw sa temperatura sa tibuok kalibutan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mount Pinatubo had a huge eruption in the year 1991!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different types of volcanoes found around the world according to their: a. activity b. type of eruption c. location in the crust
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a specific eruption event and year. It does not describe volcano types by activity, eruption type, or crustal location, which are the required content of G8-E-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mount Pinatubo had a huge eruption in the year 1991!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify and describe some of the materials formed during volcanic eruptions in the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a volcanic eruption but does not identify or describe any materials formed during the eruption (e.g., ash, lava, pyroclastic flows), which is the focus of G6-E-4.

copy.en: Mount Pinatubo had a huge eruption in the year 1991! 💥
copy.tl: Sumabog ang Bulkang Pinatubo noong taong 1991! 💥
copy.bis: Mibuto ang Bulkan Pinatubo sa tuig 1991! 💥

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A single pineapple is actually many small fruits from many flowers, all joined together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Compound fruit from many flowers is morphology; the card never describes pollination, seed production, or propagation as methods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: many small fruits from many flowers, all joined together
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: Compound fruit form is not a comparison of mammal, bird, and plant life cycles.

copy.en:
Is a pineapple really one fruit?

Not exactly! A single pineapple is actually many small fruits from many flowers, all joined together to form what looks like one fruit.
copy.tl:
Isang prutas lang ba ang pinya?

Hindi talaga! Binubuo ito ng maraming maliliit na bunga mula sa mga bulaklak na pinagsama-sama sa iisang prutas.
copy.bis:
Usa ra ba ka prutas ang pinya?

Dili gyud! Ang usa ka pinya gilangkuban sa daghang gagmay nga bunga gikan sa mga bulak nga gihiusa sa usa ka prutas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pineapple is packed with vitamin C
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses vitamin C in pineapple and general health, but does not address the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It is only tangentially related to food as a need.

copy.en: Pineapple is packed with vitamin C, which helps keep your body strong and healthy.
copy.tl: Puno ng bitamina C ang pinya, na tumutulong para maging malakas at malusog ang katawan mo.
copy.bis: Puno sa bitamina C ang pinya, nga makatabang aron mahimong lig-on ug himsog ang imong lawas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the male pipefish carries the eggs too
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions egg carrying but does not address the classification of animal groups by giving birth to live young versus laying eggs. It does not help identify which groups reproduce by live birth or by egg-laying.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the male pipefish carries the eggs too
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a specific example of reproduction (male carrying eggs) but does not describe the general characteristic of reproduction in living things, nor does it address growth or response. It is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en: The pipefish is a relative of the seahorse — and just like seahorse dads, the male pipefish carries the eggs too!
copy.tl: Ang pipefish ay kamag-anak ng kabayong-dagat — at tulad ng lalaking kabayong-dagat, ang lalaking pipefish ay nagdadala rin ng mga itlog!
copy.bis: Ang pipefish paryente sa kabayo sa dagat — ug sama sa laki nga kabayo sa dagat, ang laki nga pipefish nagdala usab og mga itlog!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pistol shrimp snaps one giant claw shut so fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a giant claw but does not describe outer body parts such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement or gathering food. The claw's snapping is presented as a stunning mechanism, not as a body part used to move or gather food.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it creates a popping bubble that stuns nearby fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The popping bubble is a sound-like effect, but the card does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It focuses on the shrimp's action and its effect, not on sound production or transfer.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: sometimes even flashing a bit of light
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions a brief flash of light as a side effect; it does not describe sources of light or their uses in everyday situations.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pistol shrimp snaps one giant claw shut so fast
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a physical mechanism (cavitation bubble) rather than an evolutionary adaptation such as mimicry or camouflage. It does not explain how the animal has changed to better suit its environment.

copy.en:
How does a tiny shrimp stun fish?

The pistol shrimp snaps one giant claw shut so fast it creates a popping bubble that stuns nearby fish and shrimp, sometimes even flashing a bit of light.
copy.tl:
Paano napapatulala ng maliit na shrimp ang isda?

Ang pistol shrimp ay kumikindat ng isang malaking kuko nang napakabilis, na lumilikha ng bula na nagpapagulo sa mga isda at shrimp sa lapit, at minsan ay may kislap pa ng ilaw.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagpakuyapan sa gamay nga hipon ang isda?

Ang pistol shrimp mopikpik sa iyang usa ka dako nga kuko nga paspas kaayo, nga mohimo og bula nga makapahilanta sa mga isda ug hipon sa duol, ug usahay adunay kislap sa suga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pitch of a sound depends on how fast something vibrates!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: research using secondary sources to identify how the properties of waves are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a basic fact about pitch and vibration speed, but the competency requires research using secondary sources to identify how wave properties are described using scientific terms such as amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and velocity. The card does not mention research, secondary sources, or any of these scientific terms, nor does it describe wave properties. It only provides background knowledge about pitch, which is related to frequency but not directly teaching the competency.

copy.en: The pitch of a sound depends on how fast something vibrates!
copy.tl: Ang pitch ng tunog ay nakadepende sa kung gaano kabilis nanginginig ang isang bagay!
copy.bis: Ang pitch sa tingog nagdepende kon unsa ka dali magkurog ang usa ka butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: with their pitcher traps dangling from the tips of their leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a specialized structure (pitcher trap) but does not describe its purpose, which is the core of G5-L-7.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Many pitcher plants (Nepenthes) are actually climbing vines
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a growth habit but does not explain adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: with their pitcher traps dangling from the tips of their leaves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaves but does not describe their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil, which is the focus of G3-L-5.

copy.en: Many pitcher plants (Nepenthes) are actually climbing vines, with their pitcher traps dangling from the tips of their leaves.
copy.tl: Karamihan sa Nepenthes ay parang baging na umaakyat, na may nakabitin na tabo sa dulo ng dahon nito.
copy.bis: Daghang Nepenthes morag baging nga mokatay, nga adunay nagbitay nga tabo sa tumoy sa dahon niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: caused by Yersinia pestis bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions bacteria as the cause of plague but does not teach that bacteria are unicellular or contrast unicellular vs multicellular organisms. It only names a bacterium, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: caused by Yersinia pestis bacteria
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe mutations as changes in DNA or chromosomes and discuss some of the factors that cause mutations, such as infectious agents, radiation, and chemicals
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a disease caused by an infectious agent but never mentions mutations, DNA, or chromosomes. It does not teach the competency's core concept of mutations or their causes.

copy.en:
What killed half of Europe in the 1300s?

The bubonic plague — caused by Yersinia pestis bacteria spread by rat fleas — killed about half the population of Europe in the 14th century!
copy.tl:
Ano ang pumatay ng halos kalahati ng Europa noong ika-14 siglo?

Ang bubonic plague, na dulot ng bakteryang Yersinia pestis na kumakalat sa mga pulgas ng daga, ay pumatay ng halos kalahati ng populasyon ng Europa noong ika-14 siglo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nakapatay sa halos katunga sa Europa niadtong ika-14 siglo?

Ang bubonic plague, nga gikagikan sa Yersinia pestis nga bakterya nga mikaylap pinaagi sa mga pulgas sa mga daga, nakapatay sa halos katunga sa populasyon sa Europa niadtong ika-14 siglo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a flat mirror, your image is the exact same size as you, but your left and right appear reversed!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about plane mirror reflection (left-right reversal). The competency requires carrying out guided investigations to describe and illustrate reflection using plane and curved mirrors and refraction using blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card does not support the investigative, illustrative, or broader scope of the competency; it only touches on one everyday example of plane mirror reflection without describing the reflection process or covering curved mirrors or refraction.

copy.en:
What happens to your image in a flat mirror?

In a flat mirror, your image is the exact same size as you, but your left and right appear reversed!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa larawan mo sa patag na salamin?

Sa patag na salamin, ang larawan mo ay kasinglaki mo, ngunit baliktad ang kaliwa at kanan!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa imong hulagway sa patag nga salamin?

Sa patag nga salamin, ang imong hulagway parehas og gidak-on nimo, apan baliskad ang wala ug tuo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jupiter is the largest and Mercury is the smallest
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the relative sizes of a few planets (Jupiter, Mercury, Earth). It does not describe the general structure of the solar system, identify the names of major celestial objects, or discuss their main features and general composition as required by the competency.

copy.en:
Which planet is the biggest in our Solar System?

Among the eight planets, Jupiter is the largest and Mercury is the smallest! Earth is also very small compared to Jupiter.
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang pinakamalaki sa ating Solar System?

Sa walong planeta, ang Jupiter ang pinakamalaki at ang Mercury ang pinakamaliit! Maliit lang ang Earth kung ihahambing sa Jupiter.
copy.bis:
Hain nga planeta ang labing dako sa atong Solar System?

Sa walo ka planeta, ang Jupiter mao ang labing dako ug ang Mercury ang labing gamay! Gamay ra ang Earth kon itandi sa Jupiter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Jupiter is the largest planet in the entire Solar System!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states a single fact about Jupiter's size. The competency requires describing the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition. This card does not describe the structure, list multiple objects, or address composition; it merely mentions one feature of one planet.

copy.en:
Which planet is the largest in the Solar System?

Jupiter is the largest planet in the entire Solar System!
copy.tl:
Aling planeta ang pinakamalaki sa Sistemang Solar?

Ang Jupiter ang pinakamalaking planeta sa buong Sistemang Solar!
copy.bis:
Unsa nga planeta ang pinakadako sa Sistemang Solar?

Ang Jupiter mao ang pinakadako nga planeta sa tibuok Sistemang Solar!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Mercury is the fastest at 88 Earth days, while Neptune is the slowest at 165 Earth years.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses orbital speeds of planets, not the general structure of the solar system, names of major celestial objects, their main features, or general composition. It only names two planets and gives orbital periods, which does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Why do some planets orbit the Sun faster than others?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to explore and record how and when the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains orbital speed differences using Kepler's third law, but does not address how or when the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars can be seen moving across the sky, nor does it involve guided activities to explore and record such motion.

copy.en:
Why do some planets orbit the Sun faster than others?

Kepler's third law says closer planets orbit faster! Mercury is the fastest at 88 Earth days, while Neptune is the slowest at 165 Earth years.
copy.tl:
Bakit mas mabilis ang pag-orbit ng ibang planeta sa Araw?

Ayon sa ikatlong batas ni Kepler, mas mabilis ang pag-orbit ng malalapit na planeta! Ang Mercury ang pinakamabilis sa 88 Earth days, at Neptune ang pinakamabagal sa 165 Earth years.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga mas paspas ang paglibot sa ubang planeta palibot sa Adlaw?

Sumala sa ikatlong batas ni Kepler, mas paspas maglibot ang mga duol nga planeta! Ang Mercury pinaka-paspas sa 88 Earth days, ug Neptune pinaka-hinay sa 165 Earth years.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plankton are tiny living things that float and drift in the ocean water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that plankton are tiny living things that drift in the ocean. It does not use a table, does not classify plankton into any of the named groups (plants, animals, microorganisms), and provides no information about similar characteristics for classification. It is merely related to the topic of living things.

copy.en: Plankton are tiny living things that float and drift in the ocean water. Many of them are so small you'd need a microscope to see them.
copy.tl: Ang plankton ay napakaliit na nilalang na lumulutang at naaanod sa tubig-dagat. Marami sa kanila ang napakaliit kaya kailangan pa ng mikroskopyo para makita.
copy.bis: Ang plankton mga gagmay kaayo nga binuhat nga naglutaw ug naanod sa tubig-dagat. Daghan kanila gagmay kaayo mao nga kinahanglan pa og mikroskopyo aron makita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: a round gall made by a tiny wasp on oak trees
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe that living things interact with each other in the natural environment, such as through competition, or predation
assignedReviews.reason: The card is not living things interacting through competition or predation.

copy.en: A famous example is the "oak apple" — a round gall made by a tiny wasp on oak trees.
copy.tl: Isang sikat na halimbawa ang "oak apple" — bilog na gall na ginagawa ng maliit na putakti sa puno ng oak.
copy.bis: Usa ka bantog nga ehemplo mao ang "oak apple" — lingin nga gall nga gibuhat sa gamayng putakti sa kahoyng oak.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Plants turn carbon into sugar and store it away in their roots, stems, and leaves.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single fact about carbon being converted to sugar and stored in plants. It does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor does it identify raw materials and products as required by the competency. The content is topically related to photosynthesis but provides no direct instructional support for the competency's specific skills.

copy.en: Plants turn carbon into sugar and store it away in their roots, stems, and leaves.
copy.tl: Ginagawang asukal ng halaman ang karbon at iniimbak ito sa kanilang ugat, tangkay, at dahon.
copy.bis: Ang mga tanom naghimo sa karbon nga asukal ug nagtipig niini sa ilang gamot, punoan, ug dahon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it is cheap, super light, and really strong
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'light' and 'strong' which are physical properties, but it does not describe or explain these properties as the competency requires (e.g., hard, shiny, stretchable). The focus is on why plastic is popular (cheap, light, strong), not on teaching students to describe physical properties of solid materials. 'Cheap' is an economic, not physical, property. This is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en: We use plastic for so many things because it is cheap, super light, and really strong!
copy.tl: Ginagamit natin ang plastik sa napakaraming bagay dahil ito ay mura, magaan, at napakatibay!
copy.bis: Gigamit nato ang plastik sa daghang butang kay kini barato, gaan, ug lig-on kaayo!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: parts of crude oil are turned into the building blocks of plastic
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the benefits of each mixture separation technique in preparing useful products
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that parts of crude oil become plastic building blocks, but it does not mention any mixture separation technique (decantation, winnowing, filtering, etc.) or explain the benefits of such techniques in preparing useful products. The connection to petroleum refining is only implicit and not taught.

copy.en:
Does oil only give us things to burn?

No! Besides fuels, parts of crude oil are turned into the building blocks of plastic.
copy.tl:
Gatong lang ba ang nakukuha natin sa langis?

Hindi! Bukod sa gatong, ang bahagi ng crude oil ay ginagawang sangkap ng plastik.
copy.bis:
Sugnod lang ba ang makuha nato sa lana?

Dili! Gawas sa sugnod, ang ubang bahin sa crude oil himuong sangkap sa plastik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Earth's tectonic plates are always moving!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to describe and explain what mechanisms that drive the movement of tectonic plates including the role of the asthenosphere
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions plate movement but does not describe or explain the mechanisms that drive the movement, nor the role of the asthenosphere. It focuses on the effect of plates on rocks, not the causes of plate motion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They bury, push, and heat rocks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe structures, movements, or events at specific plate boundary types. It only states that plates move and affect rocks, without addressing boundary types or their characteristics.

copy.en: Earth's tectonic plates are always moving! They bury, push, and heat rocks, keeping them moving through the rock cycle.
copy.tl: Palaging gumagalaw ang mga tectonic plates ng Earth! Nilo-libing, tinutulak, at pinapainit nila ang mga bato, kaya patuloy silang dumadaan sa siklo ng bato.
copy.bis: Kanunay nga naglihok ang mga tectonic plates sa Kalibutan! Naglubong, nagtukmod, ug nag-init sila sa mga bato, mao nga padayon silang moagi sa siklo sa bato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they're naturally found only in Australia
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that platypuses are not native to the Philippines and are found only in Australia. It does not use a drawing or diagram, does not classify Philippine animals/plants, and does not address terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial habitat categories.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they're naturally found only in Australia
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an animal and its geographic range, but it does not use a table and does not classify living things into the named groups (mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians, etc.). It provides no direct instructional support for this competency.

copy.en:
Are there platypuses in the Philippines?

No wild platypuses live in the Philippines — they're naturally found only in Australia.
copy.tl:
May platypus ba sa Pilipinas?

Walang ligaw na platypus sa Pilipinas dahil natural itong matatagpuan lang sa Australia.
copy.bis:
Aduna bay platypus sa Pilipinas?

Walay ihalas nga platypus sa Pilipinas kay makit-an lang kini sa kinaiyahan sa Australia.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spur is sharp and has a channel through which venom flows from a gland into the body of an enemy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes an outer body part (spur) but its role is venom delivery for defense, not movement or gathering food as required by the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spur is sharp and has a channel through which venom flows from a gland into the body of an enemy.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The venom spur is an adaptation, but the card only describes its mechanism, not how the animal changed over time to better suit its environment, which is the focus of the competency.

copy.en:
How does a platypus's spur work?

The spur is sharp and has a channel through which venom flows from a gland into the body of an enemy.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagana ang tibo ng platypus?

Ang tibo ay matulis at may daluyan kung saan dumadaloy ang kamandag mula sa glandula papunta sa katawan ng kalaban.
copy.bis:
Giunsa paglihok ang tibo sa platypus?

Ang tibo hait ug adunay agianan diin moagi ang hilo gikan sa glandula paingon sa lawas sa kaaway.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It makes your heart beat faster and strengthens all your body's muscles.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the heart and muscles but does not describe how the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems work. It only states that playing patintero is exercise that increases heart rate and strengthens muscles, which is an effect of activity, not an explanation of system function.

copy.en: Playing patintero is awesome active exercise! It makes your heart beat faster and strengthens all your body's muscles.
copy.tl: Ang paglalaro ng patintero ay nakakagana na aktibong ehersisyo! Nagpapabilis ng tibok ng puso at nagpapalakas ng mga kalamnan ng katawan!
copy.bis: Ang pagdula ug patintero usa ka aktibo nga ehersisyo! Nagpaspas sa pitik sa kasingkasing ug nagpalig-on sa mga kaunoran sa lawas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: hollowed out by the water crashing down again and again
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a plunge pool formed by water erosion, but it does not demonstrate how erosion transports Earth materials. It only mentions the hollowing effect, not the movement or transport of eroded material.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At the foot of many waterfalls, there is a deep plunge pool
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies a plunge pool as a landform at the foot of waterfalls, but it does not describe how it influences non-living and living components of the environment. It only names the landform without discussing its effects.

copy.en:
What is a plunge pool?

At the foot of many waterfalls, there is a deep plunge pool hollowed out by the water crashing down again and again!
copy.tl:
Ano ang plunge pool?

Sa paanan ng maraming talon ay may malalim na plunge pool na hinukay ng tubig na walang tigil na bumabagsak doon!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang plunge pool?

Sa tiilan sa daghang busay adunay lawom nga plunge pool nga gikalot sa tubig nga walay hunong nga nahulog didto!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh at the Lowell Observatory!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card names Clyde Tombaugh as a foreign scientist, but it describes a discovery, not an invention. The competency specifically requires identifying a scientist and their invention/s, so the card does not directly support the required skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh at the Lowell Observatory!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: distinguish among comets, meteoroids, asteroids, and dwarf planets, and describe how they help us to understand the nature and formation of the Earth and the Solar System
assignedReviews.reason: Pluto is a dwarf planet, but the card only states its discovery year and discoverer. It does not distinguish Pluto from comets, meteoroids, asteroids, or other dwarf planets, nor does it explain how these objects help understand Earth and Solar System formation.

copy.en: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh at the Lowell Observatory!
copy.tl: Natuklasan ang Pluto noong 1930 ni Clyde Tombaugh sa Lowell Observatory!
copy.bis: Nadiskobrehan ang Pluto niadtong 1930 ni Clyde Tombaugh sa Lowell Observatory!
